concept.title: What is Phishing
concept.shortdesc: Phishing attacks, common tactics used by attackers, warning signs of phishing messages, and steps you can take to respond safely.

conbody.p: Phishing occurs when cybercriminals send deceptive messages designed to look like they come from a trusted person or organization in order to trick you into opening harmful links, downloading infected attachments, or revealing personal and financial information. These lures commonly arrive as emails, text messages (smishing), social media direct messages, or phone calls. According to CISA, common warning signs include urgent or emotionally appealing language claiming dire consequences, requests for sensitive information, untrusted shortened URLs, and spoofed email addresses or domains—though artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly enables attackers to write messages with flawless spelling and grammar. To respond safely across all campus groups, follow CISA's three steps: recognize the red flags, resist clicking links or attachments, and delete the message after reporting it without replying or clicking unsubscribe links.
